Binding — planned controls are absent, not disabled. A control whose service has not landed is not in the build: no struck Sound chip waiting for 1334, no greyed Design a voice waiting for 1332, no Saved filter with nothing behind it. It appears when the coordinator reports the capability behind it — a reader that declares sounds, a provider that can design, a voice library that holds saved voices — so the structure ships once and each issue turns its controls on by reporting what it can do. A disabled control with no way to enable it is the prototype’s dead affordance, and the house does not ship one. What this turn builds now: the head, the block panel, the searchable narrator dialog with the switch’s costs, provider names, and the widths below.

Binding — the head names the reading. Play is there whenever one block has a made take and gives way to Stop and Skip while it plays; the priced read is the primary while anything is left to make. The title is Block 16 · Odile Sarn in --type-label semibold, sentence case, with no tracking — not two columns of letter-spaced capitals — and under it one mono line naming the reader by its voice and role: read by Charon · narrator, · performed under Performed, read by Anna · Maren Kest under Cast. Delivery is six pill chips 24 high that wrap, the chosen one filled, a radiogroup named Delivery; what the reader cannot do is struck with the reason as the title. The marker list shows a plate and the words it covers verbatim — the span as the block has it, never wrapped in quotation marks of its own, so “Whoever cut the tenth key, cannot become ““Whoever cut the tenth key,””; a point names its neighbour, before and the words. Under it the add buttons — Marker · Pause · Breath · Emphasis, and Sound when 1334 reports it — each a 24-high dashed pill holding a plus and one word that never part (white-space: nowrap); the row wraps between buttons, never inside one. Each is named for what it adds (Add pause). A take row is v2 · 0:04 · George · Kokoro: the version, the running time, the voice and the reader’s name from the catalogue.

Binding — a provider is a name and a place, never an id. Every audiobook surface names a reader by the catalogue’s words: the provider’s display name and where it runs — Kokoro · this machine, Google · cloud, Mistral · cloud — and, where a model is the reader, the reader’s name (Gemini Flash, Eleven v3, Voxtral). mistral · voxtral-mini-tts is an id and is never on screen: not in the dialog’s rows, the Voices panel, the door’s chips, the take rows, the confirm press or the price sheet. An id the catalogue cannot name shows the provider’s display name alone.

Binding — the model belongs to the reader. 146 refused a model on every block and this turn keeps it: Gemini Flash or Flash-Lite is part of the reader, chosen where the voice is chosen — the narrator dialog’s Reader seg (165c), a sheet’s Voice page — and only shown elsewhere: in Voices, on the door’s chips, on a take. No block, marker, run or dock prompt chooses a model. Changing Flash for Flash-Lite is a change of reader with the same costs stated before the press, and the same takes kept. Flash is offered first for a new cloud choice; Flash-Lite is chosen, never fallen back to. An existing character keeps the voice it has: nothing here recasts anyone.

Binding — a narrator found by search. 155h’s dialog becomes 165c: 860 by 640, two columns under the seg. The left, 400: a search that takes focus on open and matches the voice’s name, its provider’s name, its attributes and language, with the matches counted in it (14 of 343); chips All · This machine · Saved · Cloud with counts, a radiogroup; then the list, a listbox, in groups under 28-high bands — ON THIS MACHINE first, SAVED FOR THIS WORLD next, CLOUD last, each by provider and then name. A local voice is never below a cloud one and never behind a scroll the chips cannot reach, so the free voices stay found. Rows are 155h’s, 48 high — Hear <name>, the name over Provider · where · words, the price as data, the tick — with a grey rule on the current narrator and the foreground rule and tick on the choice. The right: the chosen voice and its Reader seg, Hear on the selected block with the block’s direction rendered and what the reader cannot do struck, then the costs as 155h states them — blocks stale, direction held, the book’s read price, the old narrator’s takes kept — asked of the coordinator on every pick and shown as … until answered; Use for this book waits for the answer. Arrow keys move in the list, Enter chooses, Space plays, Escape closes and focus returns to the button that opened it.

Binding — sounds are markers at a point. Planned with 1334. A sound is the third kind of marker, beside a delivery over a span and a cue at a point: a vocal event — laughs, sighs, gasps, clears throat, coughs, chuckles, the set a reader’s row declares — placed at a point in the block’s text and kept on the audiobook record as every marker is; the prose never holds one. On the page it is its word in brackets in italic mono on an outline, [sighs], where a delivery sits on a filled plate. The marker menu (165b) adds SOUND after CUE; a reader that cannot make a sound has the group struck and one clause under it (Kokoro reads measured or urgent · no sounds). A sound the new reader cannot make is held on a switch as 155h holds a delivery, counted with the markers, and sent again when a reader that can returns.

Binding — voices made for the book. Planned with 1332 and 1333. A speaker’s reader menu in Voices, and the Voice tab of a sheet, gain Design a voice… and Replicate a voice… when the provider reports it can. Designing (165d) starts from the sheet’s words, which may be edited here and are never written back; one of the speaker’s lines is the test; the press makes three candidates at a price stated on it, each a preview and never a take; Keep candidate N saves one voice to the world under a name and assigns it, and the candidates not kept are gone when the dialog closes. Replicating (165e) takes a reference and a consent statement in the same voice, checks both as a take is checked, shows the service’s same-speaker answer as data, and records the rights and performer once; nothing is created, and nothing is spent, until both pass. A kept voice is listed under SAVED FOR THIS WORLD with its origin (from Odile’s sheet) or its expiry (expires 3 Oct).

Binding — the book quoted, read, stopped and picked up. Planned with 1328 and 1335. Read the book (165h) states, for a reader billed by the token, the tokens in and out as an estimate, the notes counted in them, the recorded speakers left out, the blocks already made and not charged again, the rates with the date they were taken, and where the words go; one figure is on the press. While it runs (165f) the head says where it is in blocks and in money spent against the quote and Stop takes the primary’s place; each row carries its own state. After a stop (165g) the head says what was kept and spent, and the press is Read the rest, priced for what is missing alone; a request sent and not answered before the stop is counted as spent and never sent again.

Binding — a saved voice out of reach says so before a run. Planned with 1331. A saved voice is bound to the provider project that made it. When the key in Settings belongs to another project, or a replicated voice has expired, the voice is not in this project or expired in warning on its Voices row and the door’s chip, before any run, as no voice · narrator already is; its lines are not read in another voice without that being said. A press opens 165i: where it was saved, the key now, what it reads, and three ways back — the right key, the same words designed again as a new voice with its lines stale, or another voice — each with what it costs.

Binding — export needs this machine and nothing else. Planned with 1336, which finishes 146d. The sheet (165j) exports the chosen take of every block of every whole chapter, counts the rest with its dashed door, and says in one line what it needs: this machine · no provider · no key. A book read in the cloud exports with no credential present.

Binding — widths. At 1360 the workspace is 126’s. When the centre is narrower than the blocks’ 640, the gap and the side, the side keeps 250 and the blocks give up width, to 460; the gap and the centre’s padding fall to 20. At 1200 × 790 with the dock (165k) the centre is 823 and the blocks 513: the block panel sits beside them, on screen, and while a block is chosen the side holds its panel alone, the Voices group one press away on the head’s narrator. The filter keeps the chips that fit and counts the rest (+1). The side goes under the blocks only when the centre is under 700, and there the chapter is one column (165l): the view seg and Play, then the reading and the priced read, the filter as a row that swipes, the speaker’s name over a line rather than in a margin, and the block panel as a sheet raised by a press on a block, every target 44. The narrator dialog below 700 is a full-height sheet (165m) in one column.

Binding — keyboard, focus and names. The reading button is a menu button (aria-haspopup, aria-expanded) over a menu of radio items; the delivery chips a radiogroup; the add buttons buttons, named; the voices a listbox of options with aria-selected; each play named Hear <name>; a block’s state dot says its state in words to a screen reader, not in colour alone. Dialogs and sheets hold focus and give it back. Nothing here animates under prefers-reduced-motion but the play state.

Binding — planned controls are absent, not disabled. A control whose service has not landed is not in the build: no struck Sound chip waiting for 1334, no greyed Design a voice waiting for 1332, no Saved filter with nothing behind it. It appears when the coordinator reports the capability behind it — a reader that declares sounds, a provider that can design, a voice library that holds saved voices — so the structure ships once and each issue turns its controls on by reporting what it can do. A disabled control with no way to enable it is the prototype’s dead affordance, and the house does not ship one. What this turn builds now: the head, the block panel, the searchable narrator dialog with the switch’s costs, provider names, and the widths below.

Binding — the head names the reading. The chapter’s view row is 155e’s: the Manuscript · Audiobook seg, then the reading as a menu button in mono — Performed · Charon, the reading in --muted-foreground and the narrator in the foreground, a chevron — then Play and Read the chapter · N blocks · $X at the right. Play is there whenever one block has a made take and gives way to Stop and Skip while it plays; the priced read is the primary while anything is left to make. The menu, 248, is headed READING · WHOLE BOOK: Narrator, Performed, Cast as radio items with their data (one voice, notes, 7 voices), a rule, and Narrator…, which opens 165c. A choice here writes the book’s reading exactly as the door’s seg does, and is refused while a run is going as that seg is. This is the chapter’s way into Performed; the build had none.

Binding — the block panel is words, chips and one row of buttons. The title is Block 16 · Odile Sarn in --type-label semibold, sentence case, with no tracking — not two columns of letter-spaced capitals — and under it one mono line naming the reader by its voice and role: read by Charon · narrator, · performed under Performed, read by Anna · Maren Kest under Cast. Delivery is six pill chips 24 high that wrap, the chosen one filled, a radiogroup named Delivery; what the reader cannot do is struck with the reason as the title. The marker list shows a plate and the words it covers verbatim — the span as the block has it, never wrapped in quotation marks of its own, so “Whoever cut the tenth key, cannot become ““Whoever cut the tenth key,””; a point names its neighbour, before and the words. Under it the add buttons — Marker · Pause · Breath · Emphasis, and Sound when 1334 reports it — each a 24-high dashed pill holding a plus and one word that never part (white-space: nowrap); the row wraps between buttons, never inside one. Each is named for what it adds (Add pause). A take row is v2 · 0:04 · George · Kokoro: the version, the running time, the voice and the reader’s name from the catalogue.

Binding — a provider is a name and a place, never an id. Every audiobook surface names a reader by the catalogue’s words: the provider’s display name and where it runs — Kokoro · this machine, Google · cloud, Mistral · cloud — and, where a model is the reader, the reader’s name (Gemini Flash, Eleven v3, Voxtral). mistral · voxtral-mini-tts is an id and is never on screen: not in the dialog’s rows, the Voices panel, the door’s chips, the take rows, the confirm press or the price sheet. An id the catalogue cannot name shows the provider’s display name alone.

Binding — the model belongs to the reader. 146 refused a model on every block and this turn keeps it: Gemini Flash or Flash-Lite is part of the reader, chosen where the voice is chosen — the narrator dialog’s Reader seg (165c), a sheet’s Voice page — and only shown elsewhere: in Voices, on the door’s chips, on a take. No block, marker, run or dock prompt chooses a model. Changing Flash for Flash-Lite is a change of reader with the same costs stated before the press, and the same takes kept. Flash is offered first for a new cloud choice; Flash-Lite is chosen, never fallen back to. An existing character keeps the voice it has: nothing here recasts anyone.

Binding — a narrator found by search. 155h’s dialog becomes 165c: 860 by 640, two columns under the seg. The left, 400: a search that takes focus on open and matches the voice’s name, its provider’s name, its attributes and language, with the matches counted in it (14 of 343); chips All · This machine · Saved · Cloud with counts, a radiogroup; then the list, a listbox, in groups under 28-high bands — ON THIS MACHINE first, SAVED FOR THIS WORLD next, CLOUD last, each by provider and then name. A local voice is never below a cloud one and never behind a scroll the chips cannot reach, so the free voices stay found. Rows are 155h’s, 48 high — Hear <name>, the name over Provider · where · words, the price as data, the tick — with a grey rule on the current narrator and the foreground rule and tick on the choice. The right: the chosen voice and its Reader seg, Hear on the selected block with the block’s direction rendered and what the reader cannot do struck, then the costs as 155h states them — blocks stale, direction held, the book’s read price, the old narrator’s takes kept — asked of the coordinator on every pick and shown as … until answered; Use for this book waits for the answer. Arrow keys move in the list, Enter chooses, Space plays, Escape closes and focus returns to the button that opened it.

Binding — sounds are markers at a point. Planned with 1334. A sound is the third kind of marker, beside a delivery over a span and a cue at a point: a vocal event — laughs, sighs, gasps, clears throat, coughs, chuckles, the set a reader’s row declares — placed at a point in the block’s text and kept on the audiobook record as every marker is; the prose never holds one. On the page it is its word in brackets in italic mono on an outline, [sighs], where a delivery sits on a filled plate. The marker menu (165b) adds SOUND after CUE; a reader that cannot make a sound has the group struck and one clause under it (Kokoro reads measured or urgent · no sounds). A sound the new reader cannot make is held on a switch as 155h holds a delivery, counted with the markers, and sent again when a reader that can returns.

Binding — voices made for the book. Planned with 1332 and 1333. A speaker’s reader menu in Voices, and the Voice tab of a sheet, gain Design a voice… and Replicate a voice… when the provider reports it can. Designing (165d) starts from the sheet’s words, which may be edited here and are never written back; one of the speaker’s lines is the test; the press makes three candidates at a price stated on it, each a preview and never a take; Keep candidate N saves one voice to the world under a name and assigns it, and the candidates not kept are gone when the dialog closes. Replicating (165e) takes a reference and a consent statement in the same voice, checks both as a take is checked, shows the service’s same-speaker answer as data, and records the rights and performer once; nothing is created, and nothing is spent, until both pass. A kept voice is listed under SAVED FOR THIS WORLD with its origin (from Odile’s sheet) or its expiry (expires 3 Oct).

Binding — the book quoted, read, stopped and picked up. Planned with 1328 and 1335. Read the book (165h) states, for a reader billed by the token, the tokens in and out as an estimate, the notes counted in them, the recorded speakers left out, the blocks already made and not charged again, the rates with the date they were taken, and where the words go; one figure is on the press. While it runs (165f) the head says where it is in blocks and in money spent against the quote and Stop takes the primary’s place; each row carries its own state. After a stop (165g) the head says what was kept and spent, and the press is Read the rest, priced for what is missing alone; a request sent and not answered before the stop is counted as spent and never sent again.

Binding — a saved voice out of reach says so before a run. Planned with 1331. A saved voice is bound to the provider project that made it. When the key in Settings belongs to another project, or a replicated voice has expired, the voice is not in this project or expired in warning on its Voices row and the door’s chip, before any run, as no voice · narrator already is; its lines are not read in another voice without that being said. A press opens 165i: where it was saved, the key now, what it reads, and three ways back — the right key, the same words designed again as a new voice with its lines stale, or another voice — each with what it costs.

Binding — export needs this machine and nothing else. Planned with 1336, which finishes 146d. The sheet (165j) exports the chosen take of every block of every whole chapter, counts the rest with its dashed door, and says in one line what it needs: this machine · no provider · no key. A book read in the cloud exports with no credential present.

The filter keeps the chips that fit and counts the rest (+1). The side goes under the blocks only when the centre is under 700, and there the chapter is one column (165l): the view seg and Play, then the reading and the priced read, the filter as a row that swipes, the speaker’s name over a line rather than in a margin, and the block panel as a sheet raised by a press on a block, every target 44. Designing (165d) starts from the sheet’s words, which may be edited here and are never written back; one of the speaker’s lines is the test; the press makes three candidates at a price stated on it, each a preview and never a take; Keep candidate N saves one voice to the world under a name and assigns it, and the candidates not kept are gone when the dialog closes. Replicating (165e) takes a reference and a consent statement in the same voice, checks both as a take is checked, shows the service’s same-speaker answer as data, and records the rights and performer once; nothing is created, and nothing is spent, until both pass. A kept voice is listed under SAVED FOR THIS WORLD with its origin (from Odile’s sheet) or its expiry (expires 3 Oct).

Binding — the book quoted, read, stopped and picked up. Planned with 1328 and 1335. Read the book (165h) states, for a reader billed by the token, the tokens in and out as an estimate, the notes counted in them, the recorded speakers left out, the blocks already made and not charged again, the rates with the date they were taken, and where the words go; one figure is on the press. While it runs (165f) the head says where it is in blocks and in money spent against the quote and Stop takes the primary’s place; each row carries its own state. After a stop (165g) the head says what was kept and spent, and the press is Read the rest, priced for what is missing alone; a request sent and not answered before the stop is counted as spent and never sent again.

Binding — a saved voice out of reach says so before a run. Planned with 1331. A saved voice is bound to the provider project that made it. When the key in Settings belongs to another project, or a replicated voice has expired, the voice is not in this project or expired in warning on its Voices row and the door’s chip, before any run, as no voice · narrator already is; its lines are not read in another voice without that being said. A press opens 165i: where it was saved, the key now, what it reads, and three ways back — the right key, the same words designed again as a new voice with its lines stale, or another voice — each with what it costs.

Binding — export needs this machine and nothing else. Planned with 1336, which finishes 146d. The sheet (165j) exports the chosen take of every block of every whole chapter, counts the rest with its dashed door, and says in one line what it needs: this machine · no provider · no key. A book read in the cloud exports with no credential present.

Binding — widths. At 1360 the workspace is 126’s. When the centre is narrower than the blocks’ 640, the gap and the side, the side keeps 250 and the blocks give up width, to 460; the gap and the centre’s padding fall to 20. At 1200 × 790 with the dock (165k) the centre is 823 and the blocks 513: the block panel sits beside them, on screen, and while a block is chosen the side holds its panel alone, the Voices group one press away on the head’s narrator. The filter keeps the chips that fit and counts the rest (+1). The side goes under the blocks only when the centre is under 700, and there the chapter is one column (165l): the view seg and Play, then the reading and the priced read, the filter as a row that swipes, the speaker’s name over a line rather than in a margin, and the block panel as a sheet raised by a press on a block, every target 44. The narrator dialog below 700 is a full-height sheet (165m) in one column.

Binding — keyboard, focus and names. The reading button is a menu button (aria-haspopup, aria-expanded) over a menu of radio items; the delivery chips a radiogroup; the add buttons buttons, named; the voices a listbox of options with aria-selected; each play named Hear <name>; a block’s state dot says its state in words to a screen reader, not in colour alone. Dialogs and sheets hold focus and give it back. Nothing here animates under prefers-reduced-motion but the play state.

Binding · turn 185 Grouped reads — a chapter in a handful of requests, split back into block takes on this machine

Binding. Proven before it is built, by ear. Google’s speech page shows one request carrying several turns, each with its own speech_metadata.style, returned as one audio file; it does not say a designed voice (voice_…) takes several styled turns in one request, and it rules designed voices out of multi-speaker. The build starts with a probe on Ife’s voice that reads the same three or four blocks three ways — the full style on every turn; the notes once and each turn’s change; same-direction blocks merged into one turn — one request each, for the author to hear. A reader is marked groupable, and its packing chosen, only from what is heard. Until then every reader reads per paragraph, as today.

Binding. A group. Consecutive blocks with the same reader, in reading order, inside one chapter, packed under the reader’s request caps with room to spare: for Gemini Flash about 6,000 input tokens and about five minutes of expected speech. A block with a take that still stands, a recorded block, or a block held from reading is not sent and closes the group. Under Cast each designed voice groups only with itself; designed voices are never combined in one request.

Binding. One flow, one style. Read per paragraph, every block began cold: the voice was right and the lines did not run on (the author, chapter 01). So a request says the book note and the chapter note once, with its first turn, and each later turn carries only what changes there — its delivery, its note, its speaker’s note; consecutive blocks with the same direction and voice are one turn. A block’s direction, Sent as and staleness stay its own; the take records that it was made in a group, and with which neighbours.

Binding. Requests break where a listener expects one. A request closes at a scene break or heading, else at the end of a narration paragraph — never between a line and its dialogue tag, and never inside an exchange of lines — at the latest such break under the caps.

Binding. Split on this machine, checked against the words. The request’s audio is transcribed locally (whisper, as audio checks already are) with word times. Each block is cut at the middle of the silence between its last word and the next block’s first, so the reader’s own pause is kept and shared; playback and export join grouped takes with nothing added or trimmed. Each cut is compared with its block’s words by the existing transcript check: a match is filed as the block’s take, recording the request, its place in it and its share of the cost by characters; a mismatch is flagged split did not match, shows what was heard beside the words, and is kept only if the author keeps it, or Re-read. Without a local transcriber, grouping is not offered.

Binding. Re-read with its neighbours. Re-read, Hear block and Make again send the block with the block before and after it, one request, and keep only the middle cut — context for a few more tokens, not another request. A block with no neighbour in its voice is read alone, its lead and tail trimmed to a grouped take’s pause.

Binding. One loudness. Every take, grouped or alone, is normalised to one speech loudness when it is filed (about −18 LUFS integrated, −1 dBTP), with the measured values kept, so a block read on another day does not stand out.

Binding. Direct less often. Direct this chapter (turn 184) keeps one delivery across a run of blocks and changes it only where the scene turns; the chapter note carries the mood, and no note is better than one that restates it. A proposal changing delivery on more than about one block in four is held to that and the excess counted as dropped.

Binding. Requests are counted where reads are priced. Read the chapter, Read the book and their confirms name requests beside blocks and the estimate — 169 blocks · 5 requests · ~$0.46 — and the free-plan and daily-limit asks (turn 182, PR 1475) count requests, so a chapter that fits the day as five requests reads without asking. A request refused for the day stops the run; its blocks stay unread, and the next press groups them again.

Binding. Grouped by default where offered. The book’s reading gains Requests · Grouped · Per paragraph, shown only for a groupable reader, default Grouped. Progress counts requests and blocks; each request’s blocks are bracketed in the margin while it is read.

Binding. Sizes and copy. The bracket is a 3-wide bar left of the blocks, dark while its request is read. Request labels are one mono line above their blocks. Labels only: Requests, Grouped, Per paragraph, Re-read, Keep, and counts as data.

Binding. A group. Consecutive blocks with the same reader, in reading order, inside one chapter, packed under the reader’s request caps with room to spare: for Gemini Flash about 6,000 input tokens and about five minutes of expected speech. A block with a take that still stands, a recorded block, or a block held from reading is not sent and closes the group. built · driftedwhat shipped
  • Turn 186: audiobook-player.js in contracts, one module for the app and the package; Listen on the door and on a chapter. The made takes back to back with nothing added; a chapter read in part plays its made blocks, its gap marked on the scrubber and said in Text (68 blocks not read); a chapter with none is passed over. Speed 0.8–2× with the pitch kept, the sleep timer, the kept place by block and offset, Media Session.

Binding · turn 186 The audiobook player — the book as a listener hears it, with pictures that follow the words

Binding. One player, two homes. As the interactive player (156): Listen on the audiobook door and on a chapter opens the player in the app, and the exported package is the same player — the same layout, controls, keys and saved place. The chapter’s Play (146) stays the author’s check of one chapter; this is the book as a listener hears it.

Binding. The book, not a chapter. The player plays the made chapters in order and runs on from one to the next. A chapter not yet read is listed and held (not read), never skipped silently; a chapter read in part plays its made blocks and says where the gap is. Grouped takes join with nothing added (185); solo takes as they were made.

Binding. The transport is the chapter’s. The scrubber runs across the playing chapter, with a tick at each picture; under it: previous chapter, back 15 seconds, play or pause, forward 30, next chapter; speed from 0.8× to 2× with the pitch kept; a sleep timer (end of chapter, 15, 30, 60 minutes). A thin line under it is the book: chapter 7 of 22 · 6 h 12 m left. Space plays and pauses, arrows seek, as in 156.

Binding. Pictures are optional and follow the words. A picture is set on a block and shows from that block until the next picture, crossfading over a second; a chapter opens on its first picture, else the book’s cover; with none at all, the cover. A picture stays at least 20 seconds — a block that would show one for less is flagged in the chapter’s view, not dropped. They come from what the world holds — its art, the cast’s and places’ pictures, frames and takes from its scenes — or are generated through the art direction, priced as any image. The picture fills the player under the scrims, letterboxed, never cropped to a face (156).

Binding. The words, if wanted. Text shows the sentence being read and the next, from each block’s words and its take’s times; off by default, kept per device. A block made per paragraph shows its whole text for its length.

Binding. The listener’s place is kept. Where a listener is, the speed and the sleep choice are kept on that device only, and a return opens on Continue · chapter 7 · 12:04. The phone’s lock screen and headset buttons drive the player (Media Session), with the picture of the moment as the artwork.

Binding. Export. The audiobook exports as the player — player.html, the chapters’ audio and their pictures, as 174h’s web package — or as chapter files in the Retail profile (146d), which carry no pictures. Only chapters read whole go into either. Publications list the audiobook beside the interactive and the visual novel.

Binding. Sizes and copy. The player is 156’s: the picture is the page, chrome in type and icons over two scrims, play 52 across (64 on a phone). Labels only: Listen, Chapters, Text, End of chapter, Continue, not read, and times and counts as data.

Binding. The listener’s place is kept. Where a listener is, the speed and the sleep choice are kept on that device only, and a return opens on Continue · chapter 7 · 12:04. The phone’s lock screen and headset buttons drive the player (Media Session), with the picture of the moment as the artwork.

Binding. Export. The audiobook exports as the player — player.html, the chapters’ audio and their pictures, as 174h’s web package — or as chapter files in the Retail profile (146d), which carry no pictures. Only chapters read whole go into either. Publications list the audiobook beside the interactive and the visual novel.

Binding. Sizes and copy. The player is 156’s: the picture is the page, chrome in type and icons over two scrims, play 52 across (64 on a phone). Labels only: Listen, Chapters, Text, End of chapter, Continue, not read, and times and counts as data.

Binding · turn 187 Timing — a lane a voice, interruptions and overlaps, reactions, beds, the take trimmed; Arke proposes, the author decides

Binding. Timing belongs to the blocks. An audiobook stays one take a block (146), and its timing is kept on the blocks it belongs to: where a block starts against the one before (a pause, or a negative start — an interruption or overlap — down to −1.5 s), its take’s trim at head and tail, whether it plays after or under another block, and the nudge of a grouped cut (185). There is no free clip: change a block’s words and only that block goes stale; a new take keeps its start and pause and drops its trim, which belonged to the old take.

Binding. Timing, a view of the chapter. The chapter gains a third view, Timing, beside Manuscript and Audiobook: a lane a voice — Narration, then each cast speaker in order of first speaking — and a lane for beds and sounds, the blocks as bars in time with their words on them, a ruler and a playhead. It opens on the selected block, scrolls the chapter and zooms. Dragging a bar’s start sets its start; its edges, its trim; the gap after it, its pause; dropping a bar onto another’s lane-span makes it play under. Overlaps are hatched across the lanes. Play runs from the playhead with the timing as set. Selecting a bar selects its block in the other views.

Binding. Reactions. A reaction is a short sound or line that plays under another block: a sound from the cadence list (laughs, chuckles, sighs, gasps) in a speaker’s voice, or a few words the author types (mm, Ehen!). It is audio only — never written into the manuscript, never in .docx or EPUB — listed on its host block, and read as any block is, priced as any read.

Binding. Beds and sounds. A bed runs from one block to another under the voices, with a level, fades in and out, and a duck under speech (10 dB by default); a sound plays at a block’s start. Both come from the world’s sounds, a library sound, or Generate through the music and sound routes, priced as any generation. They hold to their blocks: a block removed ends a bed at the block before it, and a sound on it is flagged.

Binding. Arke proposes timing; the author decides. Propose timing reads the takes’ word times (this machine), the words and their punctuation (a line that breaks off with a dash is an interruption), the direction and the cast, and proposes starts, pauses, reactions and beds, drawn dashed until accepted whole, as 184b. Timing the author set is never moved by a proposal and is counted as kept. The proposal spends nothing; reactions it adds are read when the chapter is.

Binding. The take’s fine-tuning in the block panel. The Audiobook view’s block panel gains the same controls for one block: the take’s waveform with trim handles, Pause after, a grouped cut’s nudge, and Play with neighbours. They are the same values as the Timing view’s.

Binding. Heard as set, everywhere. The chapter’s Play, the player (186) and both exports render the timing: overlaps and reactions mixed under, beds faded and ducked, trims applied, one loudness after the mix (185). Under Performed a grouped request (185) is one turn’s audio; its blocks’ starts and pauses inside it are the reader’s, and only its first block’s start and its last’s pause can be set.

Binding. Sizes and copy. Lanes are 64 high with a 120-wide name column; bars 40 high with their words and a mono line; reactions 28 high in italic; overlaps hatched.
